classification.difficultyReason: Translates inverse proportionality into an equation, determines its constant and selects points for a reciprocal sketch, interpreting positive whole-number box counts.

content.prompt:
The number of boxes a factory produces is inversely proportional to the cost to produce each box.
When 128 boxes are produced, it costs $\$2$ per box.
Find an equation relating cost $c$ and boxes $n$ then sketch the graph.

spec.description: First-quadrant coordinate grid with positive arrowheads, horizontal grid spacing 50 and vertical grid spacing 0.50. The grid reaches n = 600 and c = 6.00; those endpoints and the origin are unlabelled. House neutral-grey grid replaces decorative pale cyan.
spec.mathematics: Horizontal axis n; vertical axis c. Printed horizontal values 50, 100, 200, 300, 400, 500. Printed vertical values 0.50 through 5.50 in steps of 0.50.
spec.answerVisibility: Blank grid only; no supplied curve or points.

answer.short: $c=\dfrac{256}{n}$. Decreasing first-quadrant reciprocal curve through $(128,2)$, approaching both axes.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}c&=\frac{k}{n}\\2&=\frac{k}{128}\\k&=2\times128\\k&=256\\c&=\frac{256}{n}\end{align*}$$
Plot points such as $(64,4)$, $(128,2)$, $(256,1)$ and $(512,0.5)$, then sketch a decreasing reciprocal curve approaching both axes. In context, $n$ is a positive whole number and $c$ is the cost in dollars per box.

spec.description: Complete solution graph on the supplied coordinate scale, with four calculated points and the positive reciprocal model curve.
spec.mathematics: c = 256/n; points (64,4), (128,2), (256,1), (512,0.5). The continuous curve represents the inverse-variation model; meaningful box counts are positive integers.
